The solution has the right general idea—examining the forced consequences of covering the upper-left square—and the answer \(8\) is correct. In particular, once one of the two viable initial orientations is chosen, the lower-left square is forced, and this fills the first two columns.

However, the argument should make the independence/recursion more explicit. After filling the first two columns, one must justify that no tile can extend from the completed portion into the remaining board; since those columns are fully covered, the uncovered region is indeed a smaller \(3\times 4\) board. Thus the same reasoning applies repeatedly, giving two choices for each \(3\times 2\) block.

Also, the phrase “top left square which has not yet been covered” is slightly unclear; it would be better to say “the upper-left square of the remaining uncovered \(3\times 4\) board.”
